item.title: Proustian 2.0

item.title: Language-Training
item.description: Language Training Learn to Read French — Book I A0–B1 Reading French Toward Proust. This section is the language precision layer of Proustian.

item.title: LTF-Chapter-005-What-Is-a-French-Sentence
item.description: Chapter 005 — What Is a French Sentence? Subtitle: Subject, Verb, Complement, Modifier What You Will Learn You will learn to see the basic parts of a French sentence before trying to interpret it.

item.title: LTF-Chapter-004-Function-Words-I
item.description: Chapter 004 — Function Words I Subtitle: Small Words That Control Reading What You Will Learn You will learn that small French words often control how a sentence is built.

item.title: LTF-Chapter-003-Word-Families-and-Recognition-Patterns
item.description: Chapter 003 — Word Families Subtitle: Suffixes, Prefixes, and Recognition Patterns What You Will Learn You will learn to recognize groups of related words instead of memorizing isolated vocabulary one item at a time.

item.title: LTF-Chapter-001-Cognates-and-Reading-Confidence
item.description: Chapter 001 — Recognizing French on the Page Subtitle: Cognates and Reading Confidence What You Will Learn You will learn that you are not starting from nothing.

item.title: LTF-Chapter-002-False-Friends-and-Controlled-Guessing
item.description: Chapter 002 — When English Misleads Subtitle: False Friends and Controlled Guessing What You Will Learn In this chapter you will learn what false friends are, why English resemblance can both help and mislead, how to guess safely, and how to correct a wrong first impression.

item.title: LTF-Proustian-Core-Questions
item.description: Proustian Core Questions Language training supports the core Proustian question chain by sharpening terms, syntax, reading pressure, and textual return.

item.title: U1｜General Introduction: From the Memory Cliché to Polycentric Reading
item.description: U1｜General Introduction: From the Memory Cliché to Polycentric Reading U1 is not a signs unit.
